newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian forces launch new round of Gulf wargames.
newsitem.headline: Iranian forces launch new round of Gulf wargames.

text.p: Some 4,000 Iranian air and naval forces backed by destroyers, helicopter gunships and fighters launched six days of wargames in the strategic Gulf on Sunday, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.
It said the manoeuvres, intended to enhance combat readiness and tactics against a mock enemy, were codenamed Salman-e Fateh, after a Persian companion of the Prophet Mohammad.
The final stage of the wargames, which involve 4,000 military personnel, would be held on May 17, it added.
The exercises, stretching from the Strait of Hormuz to the northern Gulf, were the latest mock battles highlighting Iran's military might in the Gulf.
Ground, naval and air units of Iran's Revolutionary Guards in April held mock battles in Iran's largest Gulf wargames.

Gulf Arab states are suspicious of Iran and alarmed by an Iranian military buildup despite Tehran's assurances it is defensive. They have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, a charge denied by Tehran.
The United States, which accuses Iran of sponsoring international terrorism, has vowed to protect its oil-rich Gulf Arab allies from any potential Iranian security threats.
Tehran has repeatedly denied the allegations and accuses Washington of stoking regional tensions in order to sell billions of dollars of weapons to its Gulf Arab allies.
